Rules

  • Product screens:
    • A sidebar (cmp-sidebar-nav) on every signed-in screen: the product mark and name at the top, up to six primary destinations (icon, label, optional count), optional groups of secondary destinations under a short heading, and the signed-in person at the bottom.
    • A page header (cmp-page-header) at the top of the main column: the breadcrumb path from the top level to this page, then page actions on the right, with at most one primary action.
    • The crumb before the current page is the single "up" link. The sidebar is global navigation, not the up link.
    • Detail pages open in place, in the main column. Never open a detail page in a dialog or a new window.
    • Leaving a flow returns to where it started.
  • Public pages:
    • A site header (cmp-site-header) on every page: the brand on the left (it links home), then, only when they are needed, up to five links and at most two light actions (link or quiet buttons, or a cmp-popover-menu of a few secondary links) on the right. The header holds no primary action: the page's one obvious next step is in the page.
    • No footer is required. A page ends with its content; a footer is added only when a site has destinations the header and its pages do not reach.
    • On a narrow screen the header keeps the brand and its last action; its links go, so every linked page is also reachable from the home page.
  • Everywhere:
    • The current place carries aria-current="page" and a visible, non-colour marker (weight, a raised highlight or an underline).
    • Each navigation region is a nav with an aria-label; screens use header and main landmarks.
    • A link that leaves the product or site shows the external icon.
  • Back and up behaviour:
FromBack or up goes toWhy
A detail pageits list, at the same scroll position, with filters keptPeople keep their place
A step in a flowthe previous step; leaving goes to where the flow startedFlows are reversible
A confirmationthe list the new item belongs to, with the item highlightedThe task is finished
A public pagehome, through the brandOne obvious way home

Do and don't, and notes for implementers

Do and don't

  • Do name destinations with nouns people use ("Activity"), not internal names.
  • Do keep the order of destinations fixed across every screen.
  • Do show counts only when they help someone decide where to go next.
  • Don't nest a second sidebar or add a second row of tabs to the page header.
  • Don't hide primary destinations behind a menu on a desktop screen.
  • Don't make the breadcrumb the only way to reach a top-level destination.

Notes for implementers

The navigation pattern is built from these composites; each composite declares the Basic components it uses.

RegionCompositeParts
Product sidebarcmp-sidebar-nav (nav.ds-sidebar-nav)__brand holding __mark and the product name; __group holding destinations as compact list rows; __heading above a group; __footer holding the signed-in person's small avatar, name and a quiet icon button
Product page headercmp-page-header (header.ds-page-header)__crumbs (an ol; the last item has aria-current="page"); __actions holding buttons
Site headercmp-site-header (header.ds-site-header)__brand holding __mark and the name; optional __links (a nav) holding __link items; optional __actions holding at most two link or quiet buttons
  • A destination in the sidebar is a compact list row (ds-list-row ds-list-row--compact) with its icon in __leading, its label in __text and an optional count in __trailing.
  • The specimen on this page shows the product shell (sidebar, page header and a content area) and the public page frame (a site header and an opening section that holds the page's one primary action), using generic sample destinations.
  • On a narrow screen, ds-split stacks the sidebar above the main column; product screens designed for phones should instead show only the page header with an up link.
  • Implement each region once in the product codebase and reuse it on every screen; never rebuild navigation inside a screen.
